Whereas Cloud Atlas follows six characters in different time periods as they live out their own stories largely independent of any main story, Sense8 follows (you guessed it) eight characters in different countries who, for much of the first season, live largely independent stories. The Wachowskis (who, along with Tom Tykwer, who also directs some episodes of Sense8, directed Cloud Atlas) and J. Michael Straczynski (of Babylon 5 fame) co-wrote the series with a five-season arc planned. This is good, as the first season teaches you very little about the overall mythos given how much time it had to do so. If you disliked LOST because you didn't trust they had any answers to the mysteries they created, trusting Straczynksi may be the only way you can enjoy this show. It doesn't introduce as many mysteries as LOST, but it is slow to answer the ones it does have.

It takes quite a while for the myth arc to start catching up with everyone, so don't go in expecting each of the characters individual stories to connect with the larger myth arc. For the first season at least, each character's stories are mostly unconnected.
